newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police arrest two key doomsday cult suspects.
newsitem.headline: Japan police arrest two key doomsday cult suspects.

text.p: Two wanted members of the doomsday cult accused of last year's Tokyo subway gassing gave themselves up on Thursday, a police spokesman said.

Koichi Kitamura, one of 10 members of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) alleged to have carried out the attack, gave himself up in his apartment in Saitama, north of Tokyo, a spokesman for the local police station said.
Twelve people were killed and 6,000 harmed in the March 20, 1995 attack, in which the deadly nerve gas sarin was used.

The spokesman said Kitamura, 28, surrendered to officers after his roommate, a fellow cult member and a suspect in a different gas incident case, reported to the police station. Both Kitamura and the roommate, Zenji Yagisawa, 34, were arrested.
The two were renting the apartment under false names, police said.
Police have said they suspect Yagisawa was the key perpetrator of an attempted cyanide gas attack in Tokyo's busy entertainment district of Shinjuku on May 5, 1995.

They believe he was responsible for placing a crude timing device in a toilet in an underground mall. The device was designed to release cyanide gas into the subway system, but a cleaner found it before it went off and foiled the attempt.
The Shinjuku case came at the height of police raids on the cult's complex at Kamiku Isshiki, at the foot of Mount Fuji west of Tokyo. Cult guru Shoko Asahara, 40, was arrested on May 16, 1995.

Asahara is now on trial for the subway gas attack as well as a host of other crimes including kidnapping and murder. He faces death by hanging if convicted. More that 100 other cult members are also on trial in connection with the sect's activities.
In recent court sessions, some of Asahara's key disciples have spoken up against their former leader, sending Asahara into fits of uncontrolled rage.
Asahara was evicted from court last week after shouting to the chief judge, "Go ahead and execute me."
The two arrests on Thursday leave five more Aum Shinri Kyo suspects on Japan's most wanted list.
